interactiveDemos.subject: Mathematics
interactiveDemos.studentQuery: How do I conceptually connect the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to Stokes' Theorem in 3D?
cognitiveSteps: Translating 1D boundary evaluation to 2D curl circulation
interactiveDemos.tutorCore: Every high-dimensional theorem in vector calculus is fundamentally the same statement: integrating a derivative over a volume or surface is identical to evaluating the field directly on its boundary.
interactiveDemos.socraticQuestion: If you slice any open surface into two adjacent patches, what happens to the internal line integrals along their shared seam?

quiz.question: What happens to the internal line integrals?

options.text: They cancel identically (traversed in opposite directions)
options.feedback: Correct! Internal seams cancel out, leaving only the outer boundary curl.

options.text: They double in magnitude along the seam
options.feedback: Check the right-hand normal rule: adjacent patches traverse the seam in opposing vectors.

interactiveDemos.subject: Computer Science
interactiveDemos.studentQuery: Why can't a Raft leader commit a log entry from an older term simply by counting replicas?
cognitiveSteps: Analyzing Figure 8 split-brain scenario in Ongaro paper
interactiveDemos.tutorCore: Counting replicas for an older-term entry is unsafe because a future leader could still win an election with a higher term and overwrite those replicas before application.
interactiveDemos.socraticQuestion: How does Raft solve this? What kind of entry must reach a majority before previous entries are safe?

quiz.question: Which entry confirms older log safety in Raft?

options.text: An entry from the leader's current term reaching quorum
options.feedback: Spot on. By committing a current-term entry, the Log Matching Invariant protects all prior entries.

options.text: A heartbeat RPC acknowledge from the previous leader
options.feedback: A leader from an older term may be partitioned or defunct and cannot grant validity.

interactiveDemos.subject: Physics
interactiveDemos.studentQuery: Does measuring one entangled qubit transmit information faster than the speed of light?
cognitiveSteps: Calculating reduced density matrix trace ρ_A
interactiveDemos.tutorCore: No. While measurement outcomes correlate instantaneously across spatial separation, Alice's local measurements look completely random (50/50) without Bob's classical transmission.
interactiveDemos.socraticQuestion: Can Alice modulate her measurement basis to force Bob's outcome into a deterministic 1 or 0?

quiz.question: Can Alice force Bob's measured state without a classical signal?

options.text: No, local density matrix remains invariant regardless of Alice's choice
options.feedback: Exactly right! No faster-than-light signaling is physically possible under quantum mechanics.

options.text: Yes, by rotating the Stern-Gerlach apparatus 90 degrees
options.feedback: Rotating the apparatus alters correlation angles, but Bob's isolated local probability remains ½.
